topic: Thrust augmentation and Thrust augmentation by water injection and water methanol injection system After burning operation
syllabus_extract: Thrust augmentation and Thrust augmentation by water injection and water methanol injection system After burning operation
specific_objectives: 20.1.2.1 Trainee will be able to understand and appreciate noise separation methods, thrust reversal mechanism, after burning fuel system, lubrication system, thrust augmentation devices, cooling and thrust calculations

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of PPT slides on Water Injection and Afterburning systems; Instructor supervision of student note-taking and Q&A session.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of thrust augmentation in a jet engine?
Name two methods used to increase thrust beyond standard limits.
How does afterburning affect the temperature of the exhaust gases?

development.content:
Principles of Thrust Augmentation
Water Injection System Operation
Water Methanol Injection System
Afterburning Fuel System Components
Cooling and Thrust Calculations

Mechanism of Water Injection Cooling
Water Methanol Injection Process
Afterburner Ignition Sequence
Thrust Calculation Formulas
System Limitations and Safety

Comparison of Injection Systems
Impact on Engine Life
Noise Separation Methods
Thrust Reversal Mechanism
Lubrication System Interaction

summary_questions: Explain the difference between water injection and water methanol injection regarding cooling efficiency.
Describe the sequence of events during an afterburning operation.
How do thrust augmentation devices impact the lubrication system requirements?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how the principles of thrust augmentation discussed in this lesson apply to the noise suppression techniques covered in the next lesson plan (LP 11).

pft_rows.syllabus: Noise suppression and its levels. Various methods of thrust reversal and principles of operation.
